title: 2 Samuel 19
paragraphs: ¹ Joab was told that the king was weeping and mourning for Absalom. ² The victory that day was turned into grief for all the people, for they heard it said, "The king is mourning for his son." ³ The troops slipped into the city that day like men ashamed after fleeing in battle. ⁴ The king covered his face and cried loudly, "O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!" ⁵ Joab went into the palace to the king and said, "Today you have humiliated all your men — the ones who saved your life today, and the lives of your sons and daughters, and your wives and concubines.

⁶ You love those who hate you and hate those who love you. You have made it plain today that your officers and soldiers mean nothing to you — I can see that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, that would please you. ⁷ Now go out and speak encouragingly to your servants, because I swear by the LORD, if you don't go out, not one man will stay with you tonight. That would be a worse disaster for you than all the troubles that have come on you from your youth until now." ⁸ So the king got up and sat in the gateway. The word went out: "The king is sitting in the gateway." And all the people came before the king. Meanwhile, Israel had fled to their own homes. ⁹ Throughout all the tribes of Israel, the people were arguing, saying, "The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies; he delivered us from the Philistines. But now he has fled the country because of Absalom. ¹⁰ And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. So why are you saying nothing about bringing the king back?"

¹¹ King David sent word to Zadok and Abiathar the priests: "Say to the elders of Judah, 'Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his palace? The word of all Israel has reached the king where he is staying. ¹² You are my relatives, my own flesh and blood. Why should you be the last to bring back the king?' ¹³ And say to Amasa, 'Aren't you my own flesh and blood? May God deal with me, ever so severely, if you are not commander of my army from now on in place of Joab.'" ¹⁴ He won over the hearts of all the men of Judah as one man, so that they sent word to the king: "Come back, you and all your men." ¹⁵ Then the king returned and came as far as the Jordan. The men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and escort him across the Jordan.

¹⁶ Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David. ¹⁷ With him were a thousand men from Benjamin, and Ziba, the steward of Saul's household, along with his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed to the Jordan ahead of the king. ¹⁸ They crossed the ford to bring the king's household over and to do whatever he wished. When the king was about to cross the Jordan, Shimei son of Gera fell down before the king ¹⁹ and said, "May my lord not hold me guilty. Do not remember the wrong your servant did on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem — please put it out of your mind. ²⁰ For I your servant know that I have sinned, and here I am, the first from the whole house of Joseph to come down today to meet my lord the king."

²¹ But Abishai son of Zeruiah spoke up: "Shouldn't Shimei be put to death for this? He cursed the LORD's anointed." ²² David replied, "What does this have to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? Why should you be my adversaries today? Should anyone be put to death in Israel today? Don't I know that today I am king over Israel?" ²³ So the king said to Shimei, "You will not die." And the king gave him his oath. ²⁴ Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, also came down to meet the king. He had not taken care of his feet, trimmed his beard, or washed his clothes from the day the king left until the day he returned safely. ²⁵ When he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, the king asked him, "Why didn't you come with me, Mephibosheth?"

²⁶ He answered, "My lord the king, my servant Ziba deceived me. I said, 'I'll have my donkey saddled so I can ride along with the king' — because your servant is lame. ²⁷ He has slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like an angel of God, so do whatever seems right to you. ²⁸ All my grandfather's family deserved nothing but death from my lord the king, but you included your servant among those who eat at your own table. What further right do I have to appeal to the king?" ²⁹ The king said to him, "Why say more? I have already decided: you and Ziba will divide the land." ³⁰ Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take it all, since my lord the king has come home safely."

³¹ Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and accompanied the king to the Jordan to see him on his way. ³² Now Barzillai was eighty years old and a very wealthy man. He had supplied the king during his stay at Mahanaim. ³³ The king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me and I will provide for you in Jerusalem." ³⁴ But Barzillai answered, "How many years do I have left, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem? ³⁵ I'm already eighty years old. Can I even tell the difference between good and bad? Can I taste what I eat or drink? Can I still hear the voices of men and women singers? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?

³⁶ Your servant will cross the Jordan with the king for a short way, but why should the king reward me with such a great honor? ³⁷ Let your servant return so that I can die in my own city, near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham — let him cross over with my lord the king. Do for him whatever seems right to you." ³⁸ The king answered, "Chimham will cross over with me, and I will do for him whatever you wish. And whatever you ask of me, I will do for you." ³⁹ So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and gave him his blessing, and Barzillai returned home. ⁴⁰ The king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham came with him. All the people of Judah and half the people of Israel had escorted the king.

⁴¹ Soon all the men of Israel came to the king and said, "Why did our brothers from Judah steal the king away and bring him and his household across the Jordan, along with all his men?" ⁴² All the men of Judah replied to the men of Israel, "Because the king is our close relative. Why are you angry about it? Have we eaten anything at the king's expense? Have we taken anything for ourselves?" ⁴³ The men of Israel answered Judah: "We have ten shares in the king! We have a greater claim on David than you do. Why do you treat us with contempt? Were we not the first to speak of bringing back our king?" But the men of Judah spoke even more harshly than the men of Israel.
